body:
Should it be mentioned anywhere else the docs mention `precision=double` ?

Also, my intention was only to correct the number here. A very minor change. Noting the compilation difference feels like a more significant change that is out of scope for this PR. It would add significantly more words to the sentence, so I would recommend a re-write to make it flow better. And on that topic, there's a number of things in this page that should probably be re-written.

---

My suggestions are as follows:

(First para re-write) "In computer programming, a Variant class is a class that is designed to store a variety of other types. Dynamic programming languages like PHP, Lua, JavaScript and GDScript each store variable data using their own version of Variant. They typically do this internally and invisibly to the programmer. By using Variants, these languages are able to freely change variable types as needed."

("Godot tracks all scripting API variables within Variants" I would change to) "The Godot API uses Variant to pass data between the engine and scripting languages"

(GDscript dot-point re-write) "GDscript stores all variables using Variant. Static typing doesn't change this, and only enforces type rules on variables."

("When a particular language enforces its own rules for keeping data typed, then that language is applying its own custom logic over the base Variant scripting API." I would remove this. It's out-of-place. Perhaps more fitting appended to the first para)

(Third para; "The global @GlobalScope.typeof() function" should be re-writen to either "The global typeof() function" or "The function @GlobalScope.typeof()". I would also reword the rest of the sentence to "returns the type of the value stored in the given Variant  (see Variant.Type).")

(Fourth para re-write; which I would recomment moving to either above or below the first code sample) "The Variant class in Godot is very efficient and lightweight, and has been design to integrate well with the entire engine. A single Variant takes up only 24 bytes of memory (or 40 if the engine is compiled with precision=double)." (and yeah, I would remove the rest of this para: "Instead, they are used mainly for communication, editing, serialization and moving data around.")
